body:
OBJECTIVES
- Students tell the main topic of a short informational text and retell key details (RI.1.2).
- Students ask and answer questions about key details in a text (RI.1.1).
- Students work out the meaning of new words in a text (RI.1.4) and use pictures to describe key ideas (RI.1.7).

MATERIALS
- Animal Homes reading (in the class Codex)
- Photos or books about frogs, beavers, birds, rabbits and bees
- A main topic and key details organizer: a box on top and three boxes below
- Tablets with the class activities open

FIVE-DAY PLAN
Day 1: Read Real Animals, True Facts. Compare a storybook and a fact book: which tells true facts? Introduce main topic and key details.
Day 2: Lesson activity: Facts About Frogs. Fill in the organizer together: frogs (topic), then the key details.
Day 3: Animal Homes: read the text aloud twice, then students draw an animal in its home and tell about it.
Day 4: New Words in Animal Texts: students use the sentence around a word to work out what it means.
Day 5: Assessment: The Busy Beaver. Read the text aloud twice; students tell the main topic and two key details.

DIFFERENTIATION
- Support: show a photo for each key detail as you read, and let students point to the photo before answering.
- Support: give the main topic sentence frame on a card: This text is mostly about ___.
- Stretch: students ask their own question about an animal and find the answer in a classroom fact book.
- Multilingual learners: preview the new words (burrow, lodge, hive, tadpole) with pictures before reading.

FAMILY NOTE (send home at the start of the unit)
This week we are reading true texts about animals and finding the main topic and key details. When you read any fact book or watch a nature show together, ask: what is it mostly about? What is one fact you learned? Your child may teach you what a beaver lodge is!
title: Teacher guide: Animal Facts
